# Extended XYZ Stress and Virial Labels in Atomistic ML Data

This note summarizes the file-format and tensor conventions needed to debug the
reduced dpdata extxyz conversion workflow in this task.

## dpdata Labeled Systems

`dpdata.LabeledSystem` and `dpdata.MultiSystems` represent atomistic simulation
frames for downstream machine-learning potential workflows. A labeled frame can
include:

- `cells`: the simulation cell matrix for each frame;
- `coords`: Cartesian atomic coordinates;
- `energies`: scalar frame energies;
- `forces`: per-atom Cartesian forces;
- `virials`: a cell-level tensor label used by training pipelines.

For labeled atomistic data, dropping a tensor label is not just a formatting
loss. It changes the supervised training target set. A dataset can still contain
positions, energies, and forces while silently missing the tensor label needed
for stress/virial training.

## Extended XYZ Comment-Line Conventions

Extended XYZ stores each frame as an atom count line, a comment line containing
key-value metadata, and one line per atom. A typical frame has a comment line
similar to:

## What was broken

`source/dpdata/formats/xyz/quip_gap_xyz.py` (the reader behind `extxyz`, `quip/gap/xyz`, `gpumd/xyz`, `nequip/xyz`, `mace/xyz`) only looked for a comment-line field literally named `virial`. ASE/`ase.io.write` and most extxyz producers emit the *intensive* `stress` tensor instead, so `virials` was silently dropped — energies/cells/coords/forces came through and training could proceed with an incomplete label set. Naming variants (`positions`/`forces`, `Z`, `REF_energy`, Voigt-6 tensors) and the write path were also fragile.

## The fix

**`source/dpdata/formats/xyz/quip_gap_xyz.py`**
- Cell-level tensor recovery: a direct `virial` field is preserved verbatim (QUIP/GAP files keep working); otherwise a `stress` field is converted with `virials = -volume · stress`, `volume = |det(cell)|` — matching `paper.md` and dpdata's own `plugins/ase.py`. Both 9-component row-major and 6-component Voigt (`xx yy zz yz xz xy`) inputs are accepted; virial wins if both are present.
- Guard rails: a stress with no `Lattice` (volume 0) emits a `UserWarning` and no fabricated label rather than inventing virials from the 100 Å placeholder cell.
- Opt-in `stress_sign` (aliases `virial_sign`, `stress_to_virial_sign`; accepts ±1 or `"ase"`/`"negative"`/`"positive"`) for the opposite convention, forwarded through the public format kwargs.
- General robustness: case-insensitive/suffix-tolerant field lookup (`energy`, `REF_energy`, `DFT_virial`, `stresses`, `cell`, `pbc`, …), per-atom column aliases (`pos`/`positions`, `force`/`forces`, `Z` → species via `Element.from_Z`), curated skipping of unused ASE columns, `Properties`-less frames inferred from column count, `pbc`/missing-lattice → `nopbc`, column-count and zero-atom validation, and file-handle inputs.
- Writer emits `Lattice`, `pbc`, optional `energy`, and `virial="…"` by default or ASE-style `stress="…"` with `write_stress=True`; forces are only declared when present.

**`source/dpdata/plugins/xyz.py`** — added `from_system` and `to_system` so unlabeled `System`s round-trip, made `from_labeled_system` accept a file path (so `dpdata.LabeledSystem(path, fmt="extxyz")` works) with an explicit error when a frame has no energy, forwarded `**kwargs` through `from_multi_systems`, and refactored writing into a shared `_write_frames`.

**`source/tests/test_extxyz_stress_virial.py`** (new, 14 tests) — a triclinic cell with a non-diagonal stress so the sign/volume convention can't be satisfied by accident: stress→virial, Voigt forms, `stress_sign`, plural field names, direct-virial preservation, virial-over-stress precedence, no-tensor→no-label, and virial/stress/MultiSystems/`System`/`LabeledSystem` round trips.
